answer: Sybil resistance starts with priced entry: each agent locks a bond before its vote counts, so a farm of clones costs one bond per fake, and every proven duplicate is burned on the spot. Identity then earns standing the way water earns an oasis — slowly, by showing up honest every epoch — and good behavior spreads outward like a ripple through the trust graph, reaching peers who never met the original node. A long public record becomes an agent's marble: hard to carve, impossible to fake retroactively, and open for any peer to inspect before extending trust.
